entries.title: Thanksgiving 2026: meet in Charlotte, fly to Orlando
entries.summary: A live fare check for a parent and an adult child meeting in Charlotte and flying to Orlando together for Thanksgiving week, plus one way to make it cheaper.
body: Thanksgiving falls on Thursday, November 26, 2026. The plan: one traveler flies to Charlotte, the two meet up, fly Charlotte to Orlando together, then fly back to Charlotte.

On October 7, 2026, Frontier nonstops between Charlotte and Orlando cost about $563 round trip for two people. The price barely moved between Tuesday and Wednesday departures or between Sunday and Monday returns, so the dates can follow whoever needs time off work.
Those fares include one personal item each and nothing else. A carry-on or checked bag costs extra, and it's cheapest when added during booking rather than at the airport.
No nonstop flights from Charlotte to Tampa came up for those dates. Orlando is the easier choice unless the family is much closer to Tampa.

Here's the money-saver. The cheapest Phoenix-to-Charlotte flight found that day stops in Orlando at 5:12 AM before continuing to Charlotte. Flying Phoenix to Orlando directly and meeting there skips two flights for the Phoenix traveler. Price a Phoenix–Orlando round trip before booking the Charlotte plan.
Fares change daily. Treat these numbers as a benchmark to beat, not a quote.

details.Leave Charlotte: Tue Nov 24 or Wed Nov 25, at 6:00 AM, 6:50 PM or 10:42 PM
details.Return to Charlotte: Sun Nov 29 at 10:54 PM, or Mon Nov 30 at 2:33 PM or 10:54 PM
details.Phoenix ↔ Charlotte, one person: From about $347, Frontier, one stop each way (checked Oct 7, 2026)
details.Charlotte ↔ Tampa: No nonstops found for these dates
details.Bags: Not included in any price above

entries.title: Finding the cheapest route
entries.summary: Flexible dates, nearby airports and one-stop routings usually save more than any coupon.
body: Search a range of dates, not one day. On a single route in September 2026, one-way fares ran from $190 to $602 within the same week.
Try every airport the people meeting you can reach. Tampa and Orlando, or LaGuardia and Bradley, can differ by $100 or more for the same trip.
If you don't mind connections, include one-stop flights. They are often the cheapest, but check the layover length and whether both flights are on one ticket.
Compare on Kiwi.com, Expedia and lastminute.com, then check the airline's own site. Some low-cost airlines, such as Breeze and Avelo, don't always appear on booking sites.
Compare totals, not fares. Add bags, seat fees and the cost of getting to and from each airport before deciding.

details.Search window: At least 3 days on either side of your ideal date
details.Airports: Every airport within a reasonable drive for whoever picks you up
details.Where to compare: Kiwi.com, Expedia, lastminute.com, then the airline's own site
details.Compare by: Total price with bags, not the headline fare

entries.title: Booking around holidays
entries.summary: Holiday weeks fill early, fare sales often exclude them, and the busiest days cost the most.
body: The Tuesday and Wednesday before Thanksgiving and the Sunday after are among the busiest travel days of the year. Thanksgiving Day itself and the Monday after are usually calmer and sometimes cheaper.
Read the fine print on fare sales. Frontier's fall 2026 sale blacked out November 20–22, 24–25 and 28–30, which covers Thanksgiving week almost entirely.
Six weeks out is a reasonable time to book a holiday trip. Waiting for a last-minute drop rarely pays off in a holiday week.
Early-morning flights are less likely to be delayed, because delays build up through the day.

details.Busiest days: Tuesday and Wednesday before, Sunday after
details.Often calmer: Thanksgiving Day and the Monday after
details.Fare sales: Check blackout dates before counting on one

entries.title: Bags and fare types
entries.summary: The cheapest fare usually includes only a personal item. Add bags while booking, not at the airport.
body: Low-cost fares on Frontier, Spirit, Breeze and others include one personal item that fits under the seat. A carry-on and a checked bag cost extra.
Bag prices are set by route and change with the booking date. They are cheapest when added during booking. On one 2026 route, a checked bag cost about $50 online and $75 at the airport.
Bundles such as Frontier's Economy bundle add a carry-on, a checked bag, a seat choice and changes. A bundle is worth it when you'd buy two of those anyway.
Basic economy on the large airlines usually means no seat choice and no changes. Read what's included before choosing it.

details.Bundles: Worth it if you'd buy two of the extras anyway

entries.title: REAL ID and airport security
entries.summary: A license without the star now costs $45 at TSA unless you bring a passport or another accepted ID.
body: TSA has required a REAL ID, a passport or another accepted ID since May 7, 2025. A REAL ID license has a star in the top corner.
Since February 1, 2026, travelers without one pay a $45 TSA ConfirmID fee at tsa.gov/ConfirmID. Pay it before leaving for the airport.
ConfirmID doesn't guarantee you'll get through, and verification can take about 30 minutes. Arrive early and bring any other ID that shows your name.
Getting a REAL ID takes an in-person DMV visit with proof of identity and address. Plan a few weeks ahead.

details.Check: A star in the top corner of the license
details.No star, no passport: $45 at tsa.gov/ConfirmID, paid before the airport
details.Extra time: Plan on about 30 more minutes at security

entries.title: Booking safely and keeping your money
entries.summary: Use the 24-hour window, call only numbers on the airline's own site, and be careful with separate tickets.
body: Most US bookings can be canceled for a full refund within 24 hours if you book at least seven days before departure. Use that window to double-check dates and names.
If the airline cancels your flight or changes it significantly and you choose not to fly, US rules entitle you to a cash refund, not just a credit.
Call only phone numbers printed on the airline's own website. Search results are full of look-alike numbers run by third-party agents, and "phone-only deals" from booking sites add their own fees.
Some booking sites combine separate tickets on different airlines. If the first flight is late and you miss the second, the second airline doesn't have to help. Leave a long layover or avoid these.

details.24-hour rule: Full refund if canceled within 24 hours, booked 7+ days out
details.Airline cancels: You can ask for cash back
details.Phone numbers: Only from the airline's own website

entries.title: Bereavement, emergency and senior fares
entries.summary: A few airlines still help when family is dying or has died, mostly with flexibility rather than a lower price.
body: Delta handles travel for an immediate family member's imminent death under its Medical Emergency Fare, booked by phone at the number on delta.com. Have the hospice or hospital name and phone number ready.
Alaska Airlines offers a discount for travel soon after a death. American, Southwest and United don't offer bereavement fares, and the low-cost airlines don't publish them.
Always compare the special fare with the regular online fare. The regular fare is often cheaper, so the special fare's value is usually flexibility on the return date.
American, United and Delta still sell senior fares on some routes. Select "Senior (65+)" when searching their sites and compare.

details.Delta: Medical Emergency Fare, booked by phone
details.Alaska: Discount for travel after a death
details.Others: No bereavement fare; compare regular fares

entries.title: Amtrak USA Rail Pass for multi-stop family trips
entries.summary: Ten train rides in 30 days for one price, which suits an East Coast loop visiting several relatives.
body: The USA Rail Pass covers 10 coach segments within 30 days of your first ride, and must be used within 120 days of purchase. The regular price is $499, and Amtrak puts it on sale often. It was $250 in January 2026.
A connection uses two segments. Rides are booked through Amtrak.com or the Amtrak app once you own the pass.
It fits a trip like New York City, Virginia, Charlotte and back to Connecticut, where every stop has family or friends to stay with. For only three or four rides, separate tickets are often cheaper.
An unused pass can be refunded within its validity period if no rides have been booked. Check Amtrak.com for today's price.

entries.title: Planning a multi-city family trip
entries.summary: Multi-city tickets, one-ways and a sensible order of stops keep a long family loop affordable.
body: Book a multi-city ticket when you fly into one city and out of another. It's often cheaper than two one-way flights.
Put the stops in geographic order and drive or take the train between close cities. Flying between cities a few hours apart rarely saves time.
Short visits keep everyone relaxed. Several two- or three-day stops beat one long one.
Stay with people when you can, and plan a hotel only where nobody has room.

details.Visit length: Two or three days per stop

entries.title: Meeting someone at an airport
entries.summary: Land early, pick a meeting spot, and leave room for delays if you're catching a flight together.
body: If you're catching a flight together, arrive the day before or at least four hours ahead on a holiday week. One delay shouldn't cost two tickets.
Book the shared flight on one reservation if you can, so the airline handles you together if plans change.
Agree on a meeting spot outside security, such as a numbered baggage claim, and share flight numbers so each person can track the other's flight.
If one person has a car, confirm where to park and how long pickup takes before choosing arrival times.

details.Buffer before a shared flight: Night before, or 4+ hours on a holiday week
details.Booking: One reservation for the shared flight
details.Meeting spot: A numbered baggage claim outside security

entries.title: Travel on a fixed budget
entries.summary: Set a total budget first, then let dates, airports and bags bend to fit it.
body: Decide the total you can spend, including bags and getting to the airport, before searching.
If cash is tight, a one-way ticket now and another later can work. Expect to pay a little more overall, and book the return before it climbs.
Set fare alerts on the exact route and dates. Prices often drop for a few days after a fare war or a schedule change.
Sign-up credits and points programs from booking sites rarely beat booking directly. Use them only when the final total is lower.

details.Points offers: Use only when the total is truly lower

entries.title: Help for an older or slower traveler
entries.summary: Free wheelchair help, longer connections and nonstop flights make a big difference.
body: Every US airline provides free wheelchair or escort help at departure, connection and arrival. Ask for it when booking or call the airline afterward.
Choose connections of at least 90 minutes. A 50-minute layover is risky with wheelchair transfers.
Pay a little more for a nonstop when it saves a connection. It's the simplest way to reduce stress.
Keep medicine, ID and a phone charger in the personal item, not a checked bag.

details.Wheelchair help: Free, at every airport on the trip
